cards.power: Defines the thing with an account of the event.
cards.lore: The account becomes the thing — repeatedly cited until it seems to have authority.
cards.gradeReason: Strong concept but player needs to know whose version they're playing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink with aged paper. Subject: fox writing at a lectern, crowd nodding. Mood: authoritative and slightly sinister.

cards.power: Rewrites the past from the present — so the story took it for granted.
cards.lore: The revision was accepted so smoothly that nobody remembered it as a revision.
cards.gradeReason: Say 'actually, that always was true' and watch the room reconfigure around you.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink, warm tones. Subject: raccoon erasing and redrawing a scroll, others nodding. Mood: casual, slightly unsettling.

cards.power: Dramatically alters the story over time — sometimes to protect others.
cards.lore: Everyone slightly remembers it differently, and somehow all those versions point to the same core story-line.
cards.gradeReason: Evocative but asks player to perform a process, not a character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: bear storytelling with ghost images drifting from his mouth. Mood: wistful and unreliable.

cards.power: Transforms speech by context instead of any new information.
cards.lore: The phrase lands differently depending on who says it and when. The question contains the verdict.
cards.gradeReason: Playable but relies on timing and table awareness rather than immediate embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: crow mid-shrug, others frozen around it. Mood: ambiguous and charged.

cards.power: Says 'Ridiculous!' enough times until everyone's agreement is built around avoiding the label.
cards.lore: The label 'Ridiculous' becomes the rule. Nobody wrote it down. Nobody needs to.
cards.gradeReason: Shout it. Instantly the whole table is performing around the threat of being Ridiculous.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bold crosshatch, German expressionist energy. Subject: hedgehog pointing, others recoiling. Mood: performative outrage, darkly funny.

cards.power: Shapes what is performable — and what seems out of bounds.
cards.lore: Was classified as a misunderstanding. The category was gone — the case was gone.
cards.gradeReason: Conceptually potent but requires player to know what frame they're setting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: owl placing an ornate picture frame around a scene, shrinking it. Mood: authoritative, slightly menacing.

cards.power: Locks in a specific version of events without anyone needing to agree to it.
cards.lore: Agreement reached critical mass. Nobody voted. The version was simply — there.
cards.gradeReason: Strong mechanic, needs player to actively manage the table to land it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: flock of birds all facing same direction, one facing opposite. Mood: quiet collective pressure.

cards.power: Someone who watches, attends, and records — without participating or speaking.
cards.lore: Presence without participation changes what gets said.
cards.gradeReason: Sit still. Say nothing. Watch everything. Instant presence — and the table changes around you.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: owl in corner watching a card game, lamp light catching its eye. Mood: still, alert, quietly powerful.

cards.power: Names the group by pointing to what falls outside the group — making the story hold.
cards.lore: Someone always plays the outlier. Nobody asks why they always play that role.
cards.gradeReason: Clear but asks player to simultaneously embody and observe their position.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: one animal standing apart from a cluster, others glancing at them. Mood: ambivalent, charged with meaning.

cards.power: Communicates hierarchy even when suppressed — especially through error.
cards.lore: When something went wrong, the group looked to the same animal. Nobody had appointed them.
cards.gradeReason: Rich concept but player needs to perform the involuntary reveal, which requires nuance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: fox trying to look casual while others instinctively orient toward it. Mood: involuntary, slightly comic.

cards.power: Between two groups that was never stated — and now governs their interaction.
cards.lore: Someone broke the rule everyone had. No-one knew there was one.
cards.gradeReason: Great narrative setup but demands players establish the unstated rule before breaking it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: two animals shaking hands with an empty contract between them. Mood: casual, binding.

cards.power: Maintains group function by allowing everyone to pretend something isn't happening.
cards.lore: A polite fiction that has gone on long enough often gets mistaken for policy.
cards.gradeReason: Everyone immediately knows what to perform: smile, avoid the obvious, carry on.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink, Victorian parlor. Subject: animals at tea, enormous elephant in room being ignored. Mood: cheerful, completely absurd.

cards.power: Determines what is performed — and performance changes decisions — even if audience is silent.
cards.lore: Who's in the room is never accidental.
cards.gradeReason: Conceptually sharp but the player-as-audience role needs framing to activate at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: silhouetted audience watching a tiny stage with one performer. Mood: observed, powerful in silence.

cards.power: Runs the first version of decisions before the meeting begins.
cards.lore: The real decision happened somewhere else. The meeting was the performance of agreeing.
cards.gradeReason: Start whispering to one player. Instantly you've run the scene before the scene.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: two animals in hallway, others visible through meeting room window. Mood: conspiratorial, casual.

cards.power: Changes institutional throughput through the performance of arrival.
cards.lore: Being there was the move. Everything else followed from the presence.
cards.gradeReason: Clear once explained but arrival-as-performance needs more visceral setup for new players.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: bear walking in late to a meeting, others turning, energy shifting. Mood: gravitational, unhurried.

cards.power: Performs goodwill to prevent group forming against it.
cards.lore: Nobody could say exactly what the Good Neighbor had done. They knew it had worked.
cards.gradeReason: Nuanced — player must perform warmth while obviously wielding it, which requires timing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: smiling fox bringing gifts to neighbors who smile back, slightly uneasy. Mood: warm, protective, calculated.

cards.power: Reorganizes collective identity around a problem.
cards.lore: Something is at stake — so the group holds.
cards.gradeReason: Announce the quest. The table immediately knows what they are now.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink, epic scale. Subject: rabbit on hilltop pointing at horizon, others gathering. Mood: galvanizing, slightly absurd.

cards.power: How a scene was played in a different context — context not set in advance.
cards.lore: The same move lands completely differently depending on what stage it's played on.
cards.gradeReason: Requires player to establish context shift, which needs scene-setting to pay off.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: animals on stage with backdrop changing mid-performance. Mood: theatrical, disorienting.

cards.power: Accepts and extends every offer — by accepting everything, creates a frame that cannot be said no to.
cards.lore: Someone introduced Yes, And — treating every rule as a story choice. Somehow it worked.
cards.gradeReason: Classic improv move. Picking it up changes the energy immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: animals in a circle, each building on the last gesture. Mood: energized, snowballing, unstoppable.

cards.power: Confirms and amplifies the previous scene — the last move is now the baseline.
cards.lore: Each escalation made the previous level feel normal. Nobody noticed when the ceiling became the floor.
cards.gradeReason: Strong mechanic but player must track the escalation arc, which requires scene memory.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: tower of animals building higher, each one louder than the last. Mood: exhilarating, precarious.

cards.power: Changes identity mid-scene — and the story absorbs the new one faster than anyone shifts.
cards.lore: A player swapped cards without warning. The story accommodated the new character more easily than expected.
cards.gradeReason: Just swap mid-sentence if you like. The table chases you. Immediate theater.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: fox mid-gesture morphing into a bear, others mid-response adjusting. Mood: fluid, slightly vertiginous.

cards.power: Refuses without exiting — turns refusal into a scene, not an escape.
cards.lore: The player said No. The Quest Die fell. The scene went deeper than any you had gone.
cards.gradeReason: Say No. Then add But. Instant productive friction that keeps everything alive.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: donkey planting feet, others leaning forward rather than back. Mood: firm, generative, dramatically alive.

cards.power: Returns to before the current tension — and carries the tension forward as subtext.
cards.lore: A scene collapsed. The group backed up two turns. The collapse was still there. Everyone felt it.
cards.gradeReason: Powerful structural move, but player needs scene-architecture awareness to deploy it well.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: raccoon rewinding a film reel, actors walking backwards. Mood: mechanical, haunted.

cards.power: Declares the ending — and makes everything before it retroactively about what the ending needs.
cards.lore: The Quest Die fell. The player paused. What they said made the previous hour cohere. It wasn't planned.
cards.gradeReason: Stand up. Declare the ending. Watch the whole session restructure around that declaration.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: crow at podium under a single spotlight, others in shadow. Mood: decisive, resonant, slightly ominous.

cards.power: Makes visible effort that should be invisible — and the effort is all anyone sees.
cards.lore: A player performed their card so hard the card disappeared. What remained was the performance. Nothing landed.
cards.gradeReason: Perfect diagnostic card — but playing it well requires ironic self-awareness not every table has.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: peacock performing furiously to a distracted audience. Mood: strained, slightly sad, very loud.

cards.power: Deploys humor with no cost — and removes the table's ability to take anything seriously afterwards.
cards.lore: The table laughed. Nobody noticed what the Quest Die hadn't moved in two rounds.
cards.gradeReason: Sharp systemic observation but requires player to deliberately defuse tension — meta-move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: hyena mid-joke, others laughing, something important rolling off the table unnoticed. Mood: gleeful and corrosive.

cards.power: Extends a moment past its function — draining the energy of everything that follows.
cards.lore: Everyone was waiting for someone else to move the story. The Quest Die stayed at 3 for four turns.
cards.gradeReason: Describes a structural failure rather than inviting a performance. Diagnostic, not activating.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: animals at table staring at cards, dust settling. Mood: inert, resigned, heavy with unsaid things.

cards.power: Imports a conclusion that wasn't earned — and the table knows it, immediately, without discussion.
cards.lore: It landed like a door closing before the room was finished.
cards.gradeReason: Strong concept but requires player to perform the awkwardness of the unearned close.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: lion slamming a door on mid-conversation, others frozen. Mood: abrupt, hollow, slightly violent.

cards.power: Unpacks a statement until no-one is willing to respond.
cards.lore: A player unpacked a joke for five minutes. By the end, everyone agreed. No-one had laughed.
cards.gradeReason: Playable but the comedy only lands when the player commits past the point of comfort.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: beaver at chalkboard, everyone else asleep. Mood: earnest, exhausting, oddly compelling.

cards.power: Substitutes the rule for the play — and thus the game stops proceeding.
cards.lore: They were right about the rules. They were right about what was legal. They weren't right about the game.
cards.gradeReason: Classic archetype — but the humor requires a group that already feels the critique.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: porcupine with rulebook, others deflated around it. Mood: technically correct, catastrophically wrong.

cards.power: Announces itself without action — sometimes stronger than anything said.
cards.lore: A player who had been silent for 40 minutes said nothing. The others played as though they had.
cards.gradeReason: Say nothing. The table fills the silence. One of the most powerful moves in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: owl perfectly still at a chaotic table. Mood: immovable, gravitational, charged.

cards.power: Makes the game collapse by discussing the game — sometimes accidentally.
cards.lore: A player discovered they were losing badly — started asking how people were deciding to play. The game stopped. No-one knew why.
cards.gradeReason: Describes a failure state rather than a move to embody. Hard to play this card without doing the thing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: card table collapsing while players debate the rules of card tables. Mood: self-defeating, darkly comic.

cards.power: Holds two positions — and forces everyone else to commit to one while you remain uncommitted.
cards.lore: Ambivalence holds more — and holds longer — than most strategies. The trick is not choosing too early.
cards.gradeReason: Strategic and performable but demands sustained non-commitment — requires nerves and timing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: fox facing two directions simultaneously while others plant flags. Mood: poised, infuriating, strategic.

cards.power: Holds two contradictions simultaneously — and makes both more true for being held together.
cards.lore: The more the group tried to resolve it, the more necessary the paradox became.
cards.gradeReason: Philosophically sharp but player must commit to both horns without collapsing — advanced move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: infinity symbol as a machine, two animals running in opposite directions powering it. Mood: perpetual, slightly mad.

cards.power: Creates a situation where any move confirms the frame.
cards.lore: Every option they tried proved the premise. They kept trying options.
cards.gradeReason: Devastating when landed but requires careful setup — not self-activating.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: rabbit caught between two mirrors reflecting the same image. Mood: trapped, recursive, eerily calm.

cards.power: Knows the most important thing being said is almost never what's being said most loudly.
cards.lore: The room was focused on the argument. The decision had been made in the first sentence.
cards.gradeReason: Critical observer card — powerful for meta-play but requires table to trust the player's judgment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: chaotic noisy crowd, one calm hedgehog listening to something tiny. Mood: still amid chaos, discerning.

cards.power: Interprets cooperation through others' exposed actions — the interpretation is the action.
cards.lore: The meaning wasn't in what was said. It was in what happened when someone acted as if they meant it.
cards.gradeReason: Academic title undercuts the card. Explains a mechanism rather than inviting a move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: cat narrating another animal's action while it happens, both looking at audience. Mood: self-aware, theatrical.

cards.power: Requires another player to change what you just said — the story becomes its own corrections.
cards.lore: Each correction made the original statement more true than it was before being corrected.
cards.gradeReason: Elegant loop mechanic, needs a willing partner and scene momentum to fire.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: two animals batting a sentence back and forth like a ball. Mood: playful, precise, accelerating.

cards.power: Story points to something larger than itself — and that larger thing becomes real through the pointing.
cards.lore: The fiction was never true. But it was truer than the facts it replaced.
cards.gradeReason: Title is a description of an outcome, not a move. Player doesn't know how to begin.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: storybook opening to reveal a real landscape. Mood: generative, quietly miraculous.

cards.power: Leaves a real local story for a later arrival — the gap is the invitation.
cards.lore: The space left in the story was more interesting than the story. Someone arrived later and stepped into it.
cards.gradeReason: Strong mechanic but player must know when NOT to fill the gap — requires restraint over action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: incomplete painting with a conspicuous empty space, small animal looking into it. Mood: inviting, incomplete by design.

cards.power: Gives the system a face when accountability is required — and removes it when it isn't.
cards.lore: A player drew King Kayfabian and suddenly every previous card made structural sense. The game was always this game.
cards.gradeReason: Wear the crown. Absorb blame. Deflect structure. The whole table understands the role instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink, regal. Subject: lion in crown presiding over a card table, others looking to it for decisions. Mood: authoritative, slightly hollow.

cards.power: Operates without malice and without exception — consistency is what makes it difficult to address.
cards.lore: THE SYSTEM made a decision. Nobody could object. The decision was correct by the rules that produced it.
cards.gradeReason: 'I am The System' needs zero explanation. The table knows what they're dealing with immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink, industrial. Subject: machine operating with no visible operators. Mood: implacable, weirdly clean, totally wrong.

cards.power: Makes the abstract concrete — the moment they enter, every systemic discussion becomes personal.
cards.lore: The Patient entered the story. Three cards that had seemed theoretical immediately had consequences.
cards.gradeReason: Enter as The Patient. Every system card now has stakes. Instantaneous transformation of the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: rabbit in hospital gown entering a bureaucratic office full of professionals. Mood: vulnerable, clarifying.

cards.power: Asks the question nobody else is supposed to need answered — and exposes the Invisible Agreement at the most productive possible moment.
cards.lore: The Intern drew a card, read it literally, did exactly what it said. It worked. Nobody could explain why.
cards.gradeReason: Ask the obvious literal question. The whole system reveals itself. Everyone knows this character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: young badger reading a card with eyebrows raised, professionals freezing behind them. Mood: earnest, devastatingly useful.

cards.power: Strips psychology and leaves only behavior — the story becomes cleaner and more threatening.
cards.lore: The Animal didn't explain its choices. The story became more honest and considerably more dangerous.
cards.gradeReason: Drop language. Act on drive. The table gets colder, cleaner, more honest immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: bear moving through a scene purely on instinct, others stepping aside. Mood: primal, clarifying, slightly threatening.

cards.power: Names the story — and the named version displaces the one being played.
cards.lore: A player switched to narration mid-scene. The scene became more true and more distant simultaneously.
cards.gradeReason: Step outside, speak in third person, name what's happening. The table enters the named story.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: crow narrating above a scene below, its words becoming the scenery. Mood: authoritative, strangely intimate.

cards.power: Ratifies through attention — watching confirms that something worth watching is happening.
cards.lore: The Observer was silent for three turns. Then they spoke. It reframed everything before it. Nobody disputed it.
cards.gradeReason: Clear but requires sustained silence before the payoff — demands patience and table confidence.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: owl with binoculars at edge of a scene, animals performing differently knowing they're watched. Mood: observational, transformative.

cards.power: Observes the story from outside it — and the observation changes what the story is.
cards.lore: FrizzleBob entered, said one thing, left. Everything shifted. Everything that was was slightly different.
cards.gradeReason: Enter from outside, say one thing, exit. The deck has an in-universe character card and it's a G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit in doorway mid-wink, players turning toward him, story visibly shifting. Mood: irreverent, catalytic.

cards.power: Declares sufficiency — and makes the declaration retroactively true for everything that preceded it.
cards.lore: The session ended before the story did. Three players continued the story elsewhere. It finished differently.
cards.gradeReason: Say 'this is enough.' Watch the session find its shape around the declaration. Immediate and final.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: otter standing up from a table, others pausing mid-move. Mood: conclusive, gentle, structurally decisive.

cards.power: Uses the first session to change what the second session can mean — repetition is not repetition.
cards.lore: The group replayed. Three cards landed in the same sequence. The story went somewhere entirely new.
cards.gradeReason: Requires a previous session to lever off — powerful meta-card but can't activate in isolation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: same card table, same players, new body language. Mood: familiar and completely different.

cards.power: Withholds partial access — and partial access creates more engagement than total access ever could.
cards.lore: A player said there was a card the table hadn't drawn yet that explained everything. Nobody asked what it said. They wanted to find it.
cards.gradeReason: Say it. The table immediately starts playing differently. No further performance required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: crow gesturing to a shadowed area of a map, others leaning forward. Mood: conspiratorial, generative.

cards.power: Moves attention outside the current system while keeping it in a related one.
cards.lore: Someone scanned mid-session. The game followed them home. They played it three days later with different people.
cards.gradeReason: Fascinating meta-extension mechanic but requires actual QR infrastructure to fully deliver.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: raccoon scanning a phone at card table, game world appearing in the screen. Mood: boundary-dissolving, playful.

cards.power: Makes every entry point valid — the story that follows is shaped by which door was used.
cards.lore: Someone asked where to start. Another player handed them one card: 'This one.' The session built from there.
cards.gradeReason: Conceptually elegant onboarding card — but the player must decide which door to hand over.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: rabbit looking at many doors, one glowing. Mood: open, welcoming, slightly overwhelmed.

cards.power: Connects isolated instances into a network — the network is only as real as the edges that use it.
cards.lore: Someone asked where to find more. The card was already pointing them — they hadn't noticed until now.
cards.gradeReason: Systemic network card — powerful but relies on external connections existing to activate fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: spider in a web, each strand leading to a different card game in the distance. Mood: connected, elegant, slightly unnerving.

cards.power: Produces an artifact that outlasts the session — the game continues in whatever the player carries next.
cards.lore: The session ended. A player photographed their hand. They didn't explain why. A week later they sent it to someone.
cards.gradeReason: Take out your phone. Photograph your hand. Walk out. The game has already left the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: fox pocketing a card while heading to the door, grinning. Mood: conspiratorial, inviting, quietly subversive.

cards.power: Bypasses explanation and reaches the person who already understands — the card selects its audience.
cards.lore: A stranger picked up a card. Read it. Asked one question. Not about the rules. About the thing the card described.
cards.gradeReason: Hand it over without a word. The right person gets it. Perfect final card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crosshatch ink. Subject: crow handing a card to a mouse who reads it with immediate recognition. Mood: quiet, exact, conspiratorial.

verdict: Unspoken Systems is the deck that explains every other deck — and then disappears before you can accuse it of explaining anything. The meta-architecture is the strongest in the entire corpus: fifty-six cards mapping social mechanics, narrative collapse, and system behavior without once feeling like a textbook. The weakness is a handful of cards (DEAD SCENE, FICTION THAT WORKS, META COLLAPSE) that diagnose failure states instead of inviting performance — they're true but not playable. KING KAYFABIAN, THE INTERN, SILENCE, and DON'T EXPLAIN THIS are all-timers. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: The field guide to every system you've been inside without knowing. For facilitators, improv players, and anyone who's ever suspected the meeting was decided before it started.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: UNSPOKEN SYSTEMS – The Field Guide to Every System You're Already Inside (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Ever walk out of a room certain the decision was made before you sat down, and never able to point to the moment it happened?

Picture the new intern on day one, handed a binder of rules nobody actually follows, while the rules that really run the place stay unwritten on purpose. They learn fast: the loudest thing in the meeting is the silence after the boss pauses, and the quickest way to get frozen out is to explain the one thing everyone has quietly agreed never to explain. That is a system. You have lived inside dozens of them, in families, in group chats, in every job you have ever held, and almost none of them were printed anywhere you could read.

Unspoken Systems is the first numbered Meta Deck in the Kayfabizarro line, and it does to social machinery what the rest of the corpus does to ideology: drags it into the ring and makes it perform. This is Social Story Wrestling pointed at the room itself. You pick up a card, run its move out loud like the meeting is real, and the table rules on whether anyone present would have caught the play while it was happening. The game was already running before you opened the box. This deck just hands you the rulebook the room kept hidden.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Unspoken Systems Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards across 14 tightly-built chapters, featuring SILENCE (the move that does more work than any speech), KING KAYFABIAN (the authority everyone performs for and nobody names out loud), and THE INTERN (the newcomer who reads the real rules precisely because nobody has bothered to hide them yet).
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and a table that decides whether the move you just pulled would have survived being noticed in the wild.
- The Observer Engine: the meta-layer running underneath every card. A system behaves one way for the player who cannot see it and another way for the player who can, so the moment you learn to read the room you start bending it on purpose. DON'T EXPLAIN THIS and THE ANIMAL are in here too, for the table that is ready for them.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
This is Meta Deck 01, the first node of a numbered series, not a one-off PDF. Grab it and you are on the pipeline: every future Meta Deck and thematic expansion in this cycle lands in your hands as a free update. The line grows, your copy grows with it, no second purchase.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I build these for people who would rather see the machinery than keep getting moved by it. Facilitators, improv players, the kid who always suspected the grown-ups were running a script nobody handed out. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Play it. Start naming the systems out loud at your own table. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the time it takes to draw and refine the next deck in the series.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"The room runs with or without you. The second you learn to see it, you are already changing the game."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
